title: NO IA. Why ?
author: fireweb2
selftext:
Why do I see and receive so many hateful comments about AI-assisted gaming – “yet another AI game, no thanks, bye bye”?

For example, the most recent one is a TikTok comment, and it’s clear that the person didn’t even bother to check out the game or the Steam page, but simply copy-pasted their stock response. So yes, I use AI and I make no secret of it. Claude Code handled certain technical aspects: the gameplay loop, the menu systems, the save system and the Steam API that automatically detects the player’s language on launch.

But it did all this by following my instructions and drawing on a game design document (GDD) that I’d created beforehand.

I think AI is an incredibly powerful tool, but it’s still very poorly understood.

The problem is that people often don’t realise the sheer amount of work that still goes into creating a game.

They imagine that all it takes is writing three or four instructions for the AI to create a complete game from A to Z.

It simply doesn’t work like that.

I’ve spent countless hours creating material nodes myself, working with plugins, configuring Niagara effects, debugging, carrying out hundreds of tests, and manually tweaking settings, lighting, post-processing, gameplay and much more.

  
I’m an IT technician by trade and I’ve always dreamt of making my own video games, of understanding how they work, and I find that tools like this open up incredible opportunities. I’m not doing this for the money – I’ve already got enough to live on.

Anyway, all this to say that AI is still very poorly received and I get the impression it’s ‘cool’ to slag it off. What about you – what are your thoughts?

  
My CrystalStack Game : [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5112090/CrystalStack/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5112090/CrystalStack/)

Except the main screen image, can you tell me your do you see IA ?

All assets are from the Fab

comments.author: ResultBeautiful
comments.body:
There's no point in arguing about this.   
Some people are so brainwashed that they automatically assume anything involving AI is a bad product, and you have no way to changing their minds.

replies.author: nfxdav
replies.body:
Change their minds by creating a good product... I haven't seen an interesting game here yet.

I have noticed over-positivity from pro-AI developers when giving feedback.   
  
They will say something looks good when AI has been used - a game that they would never independently consider giving their time or money to on Steam.

The bias goes both ways.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
As nfxdav said: the bias goes both ways...

I've seen too many people crank out a product in *days* that is mediocre at best, and plain shitty most often, and then bitch about how people hate it because it's AI without taking any accountability.

We want people to take AI game dev seriously? Let's all stop lowering the bar by proclaiming a 2 day effort to be "amazing", "awesome", "the next GTA XCVI" while all it is is a shitty version of an Unreal tech demo...

comments.author: Baraga91
comments.body:
I'm guessing you're getting these comments because, just based on the Steam page mind you, it looks like your game is extremely simplistic, the visuals are an odd mix of Unreal's lighting and reflections turned up to a million and the crystals themselves being somewhat less fancy - which makes them stand out.

The physics don't look exactly right in small ways (but in a physics based game, that's the core mechanic) and the majority of your visual work was done on generic fancy environments surrounding the game, rather than being part of  the game.

Overall, it gives off the same vibes as a tech demo for an engine, more than an actual game.

I'm very curious about your design doc, as the core game loop here seems to be flimsy,  which used to attract "low effort" comments that have now been largely replaced by "AI bad" comments.

No hate, just my 2c, hope this helps!

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: I agree 100 per cent, and this is actually the first game I’ve ever made. So, yes, it’s more of a test – or even a demo – of UE5. I’m working on another game that’s more advanced and technical, and I’m improving every day. But my question is: what does this have to do with AI? My game is rubbish, yes, but that’s my fault, not Claude Code’s. Your comment, ““low effort” comments that have now been largely replaced by “AI bad” comments,” is certainly interesting.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
If this is a learning project for you, ask yourself why you're putting it for sale on a marketplace.

As soon as you're asking people money for something, you're opening yourself up to critique like this, and imo it's very valid. People's reaction might be "AI bad", but what they mean is "You used AI to create a flawed product and are now asking me for money for it? That annoys me and I want to react, but seeing as I'm Average Consumer-Man, I don't know the reason it irks me, I just know it's something to do with AI so I'll say 'AI bad' and call it a day."

replies.author: Lazy_Department2494
replies.body: Absolutely! And having hundreds of mediocre almost-games really discourages even to give a proper feedback at some point.

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: Actually, I think that’s one of the most insightful comments I’ve read. The aim of this thread wasn’t to get opinions on my game – which is simplistic, and that was the point – but rather to explore why, whenever ‘AI’ is mentioned, it’s immediately associated with ‘it’s rubbish’ without people even bothering to check out the game’s page, as you did. But I think I understand it a bit better now, actually, thanks to what you’ve just said. The problem is that you’re obliged to mention AI on Steam, so I’m afraid that even a really well-made game – one that uses just 5 per cent AI to generate code, for example – would still be rejected by people in the same way.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body: God damn dude, you're even using AI to react here, wtf 😂

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: Very nice. Well done. You’re clearly exactly the kind of person I’m trying to debunk. People have become paranoid about this. I can’t prove it to you, of course, but you should know that since this morning I’ve been reading every comment and replying to them personally. I use Google Translate for some words because I’m French.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
Buddy, your reactions in this thread sounding like generated text have nothing to do with Google Translate, and I don't need debunking: I'm developing with AI myself.

I'm just sick and tired of people like you pretending like the negative reactions to their barely-a-product are just because it's AI, and then dodging the feedback left right and center when they post here to get some sympathy and feel vindicated.

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: As I said, you’ve just confirmed exactly what this discussion is about. None of the comments I’ve posted here were written using ChatGPT or anything like that. But that’s exactly it – it confirms a lot of things for me.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body: Confirm all you want, buddy. People who actually put effort into AI game dev know you're part of the fucking problem.

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: Yes, I agree. But to say that my comments are generated by ChatGPT is a right joke, and it just goes to show that people are going mad over this. Then again, I suppose you’re one of those people who think 9/11 was a hoax. But we’re getting off on a tangent here.

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: "your reactions in this thread sounding like generated text" Can I have an example ? 😄

replies.author: Lazy_Department2494
replies.body: Personally, I do not care if it’s AI or not. But low effort games attract “low effort” comments, a very typical case. The whole story reminds a half-baked bread that was made in a conveyor way and someone who is standing next to this bread and nonetheless proudly saying “But I am person who just measured and corrected ingredients, the assembly line isn’t to blame. Here is my half-baked bread”. Sure, in the end, human is the one who is responsible to make technology work for good to achieve a desirable goal. Therefore, in case of half-baked result, “AI bad” usually just means bad usage of AI and not technology itself, imho.

comments.author: Glittering-Sleep7983
comments.body:
congrats on making and releasing your first game!

I mean no disrespect when I say this, but look at your level select preview screenshot on your steam page, and look at the score indicator at the top of your game. I won't comment on the rest of the game because others have already covered the core issues, but it comes across as if you made this in a weekend. I realize you've put in a lot of effort, but it's time to be honest with yourself and look at it objectively.

I think you learned a lot from this game, because your other game is looking better. Before marketing that game seriously, I would also look at it objectively and see if there's things you can improve. Find the rough edges and polish them.

comments.author: The_Leafs
comments.body: Also isn't it a bit expensive for what it is ?

comments.author: SmileLonely5470
comments.body:
Your game doesn't look like AI slop to me, at least based on the images and preview of the gameplay. Its a simple game and thats fine.

The one critique I would have is not related to AI use, but maybe try and make the gameplay preview make the gameplay more "visible", show more stuff happening, maybe quicker cuts, etc.

comments.author: nfxdav
comments.body:
Your game doesn't look good, fun, or interesting.  
  
It's not that it is "cool" to slag it off. Most of the time, people are just giving truly honest feedback and don’t feel bad about telling the truth about products that have minimal human input.

replies.author: fireweb2
replies.body: The aim of this thread wasn’t to get opinions on my game – which is simplistic, and that was the point – but rather to explore why, whenever ‘AI’ is mentioned, it’s immediately associated with ‘it’s rubbish’ without people even bothering to check out the game’s page, as you did.

replies.author: nfxdav
replies.body:
How do you know they aren't checking the page?

As I said, it's probably because they are giving an honest opinion. And the games usually look terrible.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
The point you're missing is that you can't detach one from the other right now.

u/nfxdav is pointing out why people have a negative reaction to your game, and when  they see the AI tag on Steam they'll attribute it to that, because it's a buzzword right now. Take away the AI tag, and people won't magically be more positive about the product itself.

comments.author: DerekPaxton
comments.body:
Focus on whats important. What is great about the game, highlight that. Take away things that don't add to that vision.

The big elaborate background are beautiful but have nothing to do with your game. They read like "I can easily put this cool thing in so I did." Which makes your game look amateur or AI.

The gameplay is also fine, but simple. Like the first version of an idea. Nothing wrong with it, its just that through normal (time consuming) development these ideas become more specific and interesting as the devs find interesting ways to play with the concept. One of the disadvantages of AI is you can move so fast that you get your idea implemented, and it typically feels very basic compared to "normal" development. Thats nothing against AI. You just have to stop, take a walk and iterate on ideas because implementing is so fast you dont have time for that.

Why am I stacking crystals? What variation is there? What is clever abotu it? Even the name feels like something you come with in a few minutes.

There isn't anything wrong with your game or your process. But it feels low effort, which is why you gett he AI comments.

For example: Attach a scale to the platform and have the game be about eating from a weird alien buffet. You can get as much food as you can stack on your plate. As you add more and more food an alien chef becomes increasingly angry/alarmed.

Or, give the player pixelated portraits they are trying to reproduce with the stacked blocks. Which is especially diffifcult if the platform emits white light and they have to stack the correct primary colors to create the variation in color needed in the final image.

The speciifc idea doesnt matter and these examples are probably terrible. It just needs something to show some ingenuity so it doesn't feel like someone had an idea, asked AI to make it and now wants to sell it (which again is fine, but don't expect to impress many people by it).

comments.author: Sleepnotdeading
comments.body: I don’t think gamers or developers much like how the Steam store has been overrun with games that look like they were made in a weekend.  The thing they mostly have in common at this point is they were all made using AI.  So… stands to reason that, for gaming at the moment, AI is bad, because without it these bad games wouldn’t exist
